text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.3% today as oil prices remained elevated following geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Over the past week, a Houthi drone attack damaged Saudi Arabia's critical East-West pipeline, temporarily disrupting crude exports and pushing U.S. oil prices above $105 per barrel on September 15th. Though the U.S. Energy Secretary indicated the pipeline would restart within days (which appears to have happened, as prices fell back to $97.26 today), the uncertainty around supply disruptions kept prices well above their pre-attack levels and supported energy stocks like ConocoPhillips.

The company also benefits from the wider gap between U.S. and global oil prices—U.S. crude at $97.26 versus Brent at $109.51—which reflects ongoing supply pressures and geopolitical risk premiums. For an integrated oil producer with international operations and refining capacity, higher crude prices and elevated price spreads both improve margins and profitability.
